clue.text: Symbolic comb good for parting a hank that's plaited

indicators.note: something parting a bundle splits it and sits in the gap it opens
plaited hair is woven over and under, so these letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: the words taken as written, to be rearranged
G is the usual abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A ceremonial comb is just the thing for dividing a plaited hank of hair.
explanation.walkthrough: KANGHA: the scrambled letters of A HANK, split by G. The kangha is one of the five articles of faith a Sikh wears.
explanation.definitionFit: The kangha is the small wooden comb a Sikh carries as a religious symbol, one of the five Ks.

clue.text: NZ bird sounding (almost) like a dove

indicators.note: sounding like means said aloud it matches, and the bracketed almost admits the match is near rather than exact

parts.note: a dove's call is a repeated coo

explanation.surface: A New Zealand bird with a call close to a dove's.
explanation.walkthrough: The kuku is the New Zealand wood pigeon, itself a dove, so its Maori name echoing a dove's double coo is doubly apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Kuku is the Maori name for the New Zealand pigeon, a large native fruit-eating bird.

clue.text: Obsession with counting things

parts.note: surface reading: a fixation on things that matter or count; setter's reading: a compulsion to tally objects, built from Greek 'number' plus 'madness'

explanation.walkthrough: This was the month's competition word: Azed prints only a definition, and entrants submit their own clue for it. The word is Greek arithmos, number, plus mania.
explanation.definitionFit: Arithmomania is a psychiatric term for a compulsive urge to count objects or actions, often seen in obsessive disorders.

clue.text: No saint is desecrated by such heathens

indicators.note: desecrating something spoils its sacred form, so these letters are wrecked and rebuilt

parts.note: the words taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Pagans are the sort who would profane the memory of a saint.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Bible, 'the nations' are the Gentiles, those outside the faith; 'such' points back to the desecrators in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: In biblical usage the nations are the Gentiles or heathen peoples, as opposed to the chosen people of Israel.

clue.text: Axis formed in history — and then Germany

parts.note: the letters sit across the end of 'then' and the start of 'Germany'

explanation.walkthrough: The WWII Axis is a red herring. Henge is an obsolete form of hinge, an axis on which something turns; 'history' marks it as old.
explanation.definitionFit: In old usage henge meant hinge, the pivot or axis on which a door or lid swings.

clue.text: Tar I blended with grey natural sulphide

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: Argyrite is a dated name for argentite, from Greek argyros, silver.
explanation.definitionFit: Argyrite is silver sulphide occurring as a mineral, a dark grey ore of silver found in nature.

clue.text: United lead, a work of art to seethe from below?

parts.note: U is the standard abbreviation for United, as in football team names
Pb is the chemical symbol for lead

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition read as the word's parts: up plus boil, boiling up from beneath.
explanation.definitionFit: To upboil is to boil up, a liquid seething as bubbles rise from the bottom of the pot.

clue.text: One writing about bit of rock, object turning up in prehistoric time

the first letter of rock

explanation.definitionFit: The Permian is the last geological period of the Palaeozoic era, roughly 299 to 252 million years ago.

clue.text: Pale blue pants concealing worker's muscle

the worker ant, a crossword staple

clue.text: Everyone's turned up following old crock

clue.text: Abuse male patients having to stand inside with temperature

clue.text: Dress machine's cut in length of thick cotton

clue.text: Unwillingness to speak, ignoring extreme limits … of this once?

explanation.definitionFit: Utis is an obsolete Shakespearean word for noisy merriment or confusion, the opposite of silence.
